corrected_verdict:
PARTIALLY_KNOWN, with a different split from the checker's.
- Known at both ends:
  - b=nu: Morwani App. F.1 eqs. (6)-(9) for n=2; Li et al. Lemmas D.7-D.8 for general n.
  - b=2: Gunasekar et al. 2018 Lemma 7. The minimum squared l2 weight norm needed to produce a given product of L Fourier transforms is L||beta^||_{2/L}^{2/L}. The proof is AM-GM at each Fourier coordinate, and equality holds for any number of active frequencies. This is C_2, including the "several frequencies at no extra cost at b=2" remark.
- The middle range 2<b<nu takes one line: ||x||_{b/2} <= ||x||_1 gives C_b = C_2^{b/2}. So the value B_p does not depend on b, and this is not a separate contribution.
- What is new: transferring this to the modular margin through the diagonal mode beta_j, using the budget as the input to Gamma_s, and the ReLU bound. But the ReLU bound as written (C_2 <= p^{-n}/2) is false for n>=2. The paper's own argument gives C_2 <= 1/(2p).
- The power-neuron bound "<= n! B_p" is actually "=" at every b in [2, nu] (checked numerically).
issues:
1. The checker's two citations are correct; I re-fetched both.
- Morwani et al.: arXiv abs page says "Accepted as Spotlight at ICLR 2024". The single-neuron computation is App. F ("Proofs for cyclic groups (Theorem 7)"), subsection F.1, eqs. (4)-(9): QM-GM in eq. (9), Plancherel, Cauchy-Schwarz with ||z||_2 <= ||z||_1, value sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)), equality only for a single frequency. Lemma 18 (groups) uses Cauchy-Schwarz plus AM-GM.
- Li et al.: the PMLR page confirms AISTATS 2025, PMLR 258, pp. 523-531. Lemma D.7 gives k!/((p-1)p^k) sum_j w^(-j) prod u^_i(j). Lemma D.8 (App. D.5) uses QM-GM plus ||z||_2 <= ||z||_1 and gets 2(k!)/((2k+2)^{(k+1)/2}(p-1)p^{(k-1)/2}). This equals n! B_p p/(p-1).
- Both papers say they cover only L_{2,nu}. Morwani Sec. 3: "we will primarily focus on maximum margin with respect to L2,nu norm"; Sec. 7: "Our proof holds for ... L2,nu norm".
- li2025nsum is in refs.bib but is cited nowhere in the sections (only the TODO at intro.tex:22). This is confirmed.

2. Prior art the checker missed: Gunasekar, Lee, Soudry, Srebro, NeurIPS 2018 (arXiv 1806.00468), Lemma 7 and Lemma 6 (proof in App. D, eq. 87).
- R_Pconv(beta) = min ||w||_2^2 = L||beta^||_{2/L}^{2/L}, where beta^ = diag(w^_1)...w^_L.
- The proof is AM-GM at each Fourier coordinate plus the fact that the DFT preserves the l2 norm. Equality holds with balanced moduli on any support.
- A product neuron's beta_j is a product of nu Fourier transforms at the same frequency. So C_2, with its equality case and the exponent 2/nu (approach.tex l.42), is this lemma up to the p/2 Parseval factor and the 2p^{-nu} normalisation.
- The checker's "new: b<nu generalisation; neuron can carry many frequencies at b=2" is therefore overstated. The middle range follows from b=2 in one line (C_b = C_2^{b/2}).

3. A third instance of the b=nu computation: Kunin et al., AGF (arXiv 2506.06489; arXiv comment says NeurIPS 2025), Theorem 5.1. They maximise a single quadratic neuron on the unit sphere for modular addition. The maximisers are single-frequency cosines with amplitude sqrt(2/(3p)), and the maximum value is 2/(27p^3)|x^[xi]|^3. Citing it is optional.

4. Side finding: the ReLU bound at appendix.tex l.283 is wrong.
- The paper's claim sum_{F_p}|h^(j..j)w^(j)| <= (p/4)||omega||^2 should read (p^n/4)||omega||^2.
- Parseval on Z_p^n gives sum_{F_p}|h^(j..j)|^2 <= p^{2n}Var(h)/2 <= p^{2n-1}||u||^2/2.
- Hence C_2 <= 1/(2p), not p^{-n}/2. The two agree only at n=1.
- Numerical counterexample at p=7, n=2. I computed beta_j two independent ways: the FFT formula and a direct time-domain eta(delta); they agree to 1e-16. A random hill-climb reaches sum_j|beta_j|/||omega||^2 = 0.0154, which exceeds p^{-2}/2 = 0.0102 and is within 1/(2p) = 0.0714.
- Only the constant is affected; the qualitative b=nu / flat-maximiser statement still stands.
- The checker's recommendation to "keep C_2 <= p^{-n}/2 as ours" would leave the error in place. The corrected bound still has no ML precedent that I found.

5. Power neuron. Checked numerically at (p,n) = (7,2) and (5,3): beta_j(power) = n! beta_j(product) exactly for random weights. A balanced single-frequency cosine neuron attains n! B_p at b in {2, 2.5, 3} (n=2) and {2, 3, 4} (n=3). So "<=" can be stated as "=". The checker's suggestion 3 is correct.

6. Searches that found nothing for a single-neuron budget with b<nu, or any ReLU budget:
- Mohamadi et al. ICML 2024 (l_inf margins)
- Tian NeurIPS 2025 (CoGS)
- Doshi et al. 2024 (constructions only)
- Huang & Li 2025 (2511.23443)
- He et al. 2026 (2602.16849)
- Pracher et al. 2026 (2609.26679)
- Tan et al. 2026 (2606.05863)
- Jagadeesan et al. COLT 2022 (adjacent: nuclear norm / l_{2,1} of Fourier coefficients; relevant to u8, not R6)

WebSearch was exhausted, and the Semantic Scholar and dblp APIs rate-limited me, so I searched through arXiv's own search page and fetched pages directly.

Pinpoint recommendation: cite Morwani as "App. F.1, eqs. (6)-(9)" (arXiv v2 numbering).

extra_citations.why: Lemma 7 (and Lemma 6), proof in App. D eq. (87): min ||w||_2^2 subject to a product of L Fourier transforms equalling beta^ is L||beta^||_{2/L}^{2/L}, by AM-GM at each Fourier coordinate, with equality on any support. This is the b=2 single-neuron budget C_2, including the 'several frequencies at no extra cost at b=2' remark and the exponent 2/nu in approach.tex l.42. Cite it in approach.tex l.54-58 next to Morwani and Li: 'at b=2 this is the l_{2/nu} representation cost of a product of Fourier transforms (Gunasekar et al., 2018, Lemma 7)'.

Optional. Theorem 5.1 solves the same single quadratic neuron maximisation on the unit sphere for modular addition, with a weighted utility. The maximisers are single-frequency cosines with amplitude sqrt(2/(3p)), and the maximum is 2/(27p^3)|x^[xi]|^3. It is further evidence that the b=nu computation is standard. The venue comes from the arXiv comment ('NeurIPS 2025'); I did not see a proceedings page.
